applicability_resolution.note: All six trigger conditions were resolved before any sub-element was scored, using fields belonging to elements other than the one being gated (anti-circular rule). Element 4 was gated per sub-element, not once for the whole element (#1060).

conditions.condition: Datasets shared and available for reuse
conditions.evidence: distribution_formats populated (format ZIP, media_type application/zip, with programmatic access described via the Dataverse Data Access API); page resolves to https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/dataset.xhtml?persistentId=doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C; license CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 explicitly permits share and adapt; all ten archives listed with public file access.

description (E1) names only MDA-MB-468 breast cancer cells and KOLF2.1J induced pluripotent stem cells, i.e. established cell lines. keywords (E1) are modality, cell-line, drug and subject-category terms ('Medicine, Health and Life Sciences' is a Dataverse subject facet, not a participant signal); no participant, patient, cohort, enrollment or clinical-trial term appears. collection_mechanisms (E8) describe AP-MS, SEC-MS, immunofluorescence confocal microscopy and CRISPRi screens on cultured lines, with no recruitment of human participants. direct_collection.is_direct is false with the statement that data were not collected from individuals.
conditions.gates: Element 4 sub-elements 3, 4 and 5 (set not applicable); contributes one disjunct to sub-elements 1 and 2

conditions.evidence: confidential_elements (the confidentiality-level field family, E2) states confidential_elements_present true with a temporary pre-publication embargo on the perturb-seq components in KOLF2.1J iPSCs and MDA-MB-468 cells. ip_restrictions (E2 sub-element 1) states that commercial use requires separate license negotiation with UCSD, Stanford and/or UCSF, and that copyright is held by the Regents of the University of California except for Stanford-held spatial-proteomics image data. These are constraints that actually apply, not a record that no restriction applies (#1060).

conditions.condition: Software tools produced as dataset output
conditions.evidence: external_resources (E10) names the Cell Mapping Toolkit / CM4AI data integration pipeline software released under a BSD-3 license via GitHub with production-ready tools archived in Zenodo, and the FAIRSCAPE AI-readiness framework at https://fairscape.github.io released under MIT. A code repository is referenced from a field outside Element 8.

conditions.condition: Data collection identified AND datasets shared
conditions.evidence: acquisition_methods and collection_mechanisms are both populated with instrument-level detail, and the shared condition above is met.

citation carries the full Dataverse citation with DOI; external_resources carries two preprint references with DOIs (10.1101/2024.05.21.589311 and, under existing_uses, 10.1101/2024.11.03.621734). The shared condition is met.

issues_detected.description: The June 2026 release is recorded at version '2.0' while version_access lists both the October 2025 release (doi 10.18130/V3/K7TGEM) and the June 2025 release (doi 10.18130/V3/F3TD5R) at Dataverse version 2.1. A newer release therefore carries a lower Dataverse version number than its two predecessors. Each release is a separate Dataverse dataset with its own DOI and its own version counter, so this is not strictly contradictory, but the record does not say so and a reader comparing version numbers across releases will be misled.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add a version_details sentence stating that the Dataverse version counter is per-DOI and does not order releases, so that release ordering is read from the release names and DOIs rather than from the version numbers.

issues_detected.description: Three immunofluorescence archives carry issued 2026-07-15, later than the dataset's own issued date of 2026-06-17 and later than the version 2.0 publication. The record flags this in source_caveats but does not reconcile it, so the temporal ordering of dataset publication and file publication remains inverted in the data as recorded.
issues_detected.recommendation: Record the July 2026 file additions as a distinct distribution event, or note that the Dataverse dataset publication date is the version-2.0 date and that files may be added to a published version afterwards.

issues_detected.description: The technical-processing account is almost entirely inferential. preprocessing_strategies holds a single entry that is inferred from archive file naming (cm4ai_perturb-seq_KOLF2_cell_atlas.zip alongside cm4ai_perturb-seq_KOLF2_raw_sra.zip), with the record itself stating that the June 2026 listing carries no per-file processing description. The second acquisition_methods entry is inferred the same way. No cleaning, labeling, annotation-quality, machine-annotation or imputation information is present.
issues_detected.recommendation: Where the release listing is silent, cite the RO-Crate provenance graphs packaged with the release, which the record already identifies as carrying computation provenance, rather than leaving processing documented only by an inference from file names.

issues_detected.description: Distribution is documented only at the container level. format is ZIP and media_type is application/zip for the dataset and for all ten archives, with no encoding and no statement of what data format the archives contain (image format for the 12.6 GB of immunofluorescence data, mass-spectrometry format for the SEC-MS and AP-MS archives, matrix or h5ad format for the perturbation atlas). A reuser cannot determine from the record what they will be able to read after unzipping.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add the internal data format for each archive alongside the ZIP container, and add character encoding for any tabular or text payload.

issues_detected.description: No variable-level metadata anywhere in the record: variables is absent and is_tabular is absent. The instances block gives five instance types with B2AI substrate and topic CURIEs, which describes modality rather than variables, columns or measured fields. For a release comprising perturbation transcriptomics, elution profiles and imaging, the absence of any data dictionary is the principal barrier to integration with other datasets.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add variable-level entries for at least the tabular components, with identifiers and descriptions, or point to the per-archive data dictionaries inside the release metadata archive.

issues_detected.description: The University of Virginia funder entry gives 'Frederick Thomas Fund' in the grant_number slot. That is a fund name, not an award identifier, so the slot's declared semantics are not honoured. The record's own note states that no numeric identifier is given, which is honest but leaves a non-identifier in an identifier field.
issues_detected.recommendation: Move the fund name to the grant notes or to a grant name slot and leave grant_number absent when no award number exists.

issues_detected.description: is_deidentified states a deidentification rationale rather than a named method: 'De-identified Samples: Yes' from the release record, plus the preprint's statement that the data are non-clinical, from tissue cultures, and cannot be matched with current knowledge to a human subject. No standard method (HIPAA Safe Harbor, Expert Determination, k-anonymity) is named. For commercially sourced established cell lines this is the semantically appropriate account, and the sourcing to ATCC and HipSci is given, so the claim is supportable, but it is a provenance argument rather than a deidentification procedure.
issues_detected.recommendation: State explicitly that no deidentification procedure was applied because the material is commercially distributed de-identified cell line stock, which is a stronger and clearer claim than 'considered to be de-identified'.

issues_detected.description: Sample and instance counts for this specific release are not asserted. notes carries project-wide figures (1,374 protein interactions, 53,788 immunofluorescent images, 7,023 proteins, 11,739 genes, 21.4 TB) that source_caveats explicitly reads as cumulative across all CM4AI streams by inference, and sampling_strategies flags the 200-gene and 523-protein figures as portal-level statements not asserted for this release. Extent for the June 2026 release itself is therefore given only as ten archives with byte sizes plus the 11,739 targeted genes for the KOLF2.1J atlas.
issues_detected.recommendation: Report per-archive instance counts for this release where they can be established, and keep the project-wide figures clearly separated from release-level extent.

semantic_insights: The DOI prefix 10.18130 is the University of Virginia Library Dataverse (LibraData), which matches the stated publisher, the page URL host dataverse.lib.virginia.edu, and the citation's named repository. Identifier, landing page and citation are mutually corroborating.

The id is written in CURIE form (doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C) rather than as a resolver URL, and every file_collections and resources id is a fragment on that same record id, so the identifier graph is internally rooted and consistent.

Both cell lines carry Cellosaurus RRIDs that resolve to the named lines: RRID:CVCL_0419 is MDA-MB-468 and RRID:CVCL_B5P3 is KOLF2.1J. The RRID namespace is CVCL rather than SCR or AB, which is the correct namespace for a cell line.

The four human-subjects and privacy flags are mutually consistent and all correct for a cell-line dataset: human_subject_research.involves_human_subjects false, direct_collection.is_direct false with the explicit statement that data were not collected from individuals, sensitive_elements_present false, and is_deidentified.identifiable_elements_present false.

known_biases correctly identifies the representation limit that a cell-line dataset actually carries, naming the donor characteristics of both lines (a 51-year-old black female with metastatic mammary adenocarcinoma for MDA-MB-468, a healthy male Northern European donor for KOLF2.1J) as the source of the bias, and mapping it to the RAI-aligned representation_bias category.

Both NIH award numbers parse correctly: 1OT2OD032742-01 is type 1, activity OT2, institute OD, serial 032742, support year 01, and matches the RePORTER core project number OT2OD032742 quoted in the same note; 5U54HG012513-02 is type 5, activity U54, institute HG.

total_file_count of 10 reconciles exactly with the sum of file_collections file_count values (2 AP-MS, 3 immunofluorescence, 2 SEC-MS, 1 perturbation atlas, 1 raw sequence, 1 metadata), and each of the ten resources carries an MD5 checksum.

The embargo recorded in confidential_elements applies to the external perturb-seq data links, while data_governance states that all ten archives in this release are listed with public file access. The record distinguishes the two rather than conflating them, so the apparent tension between an embargo and open distribution is resolved in the text.

The date conflict between the CM4AI portal ('Released on: June 17, 2025') and the Dataverse record (2026-06-17) is surfaced, ranked and resolved in source_caveats, with the losing value retained as a recorded conflict rather than discarded.

Provenance is documented in both directions: upstream to the two cell lines with RRIDs and repository access terms, and outward to the MassIVE mass-spectrometry deposits and the Figshare perturbation atlas, so the raw data underlying the distributed archives is locatable.

conforms_to_standard RO_CRATE together with conforms_to naming FAIRSCAPE provenance graphs, conforms_to_schema pointing at the Bridge2AI data-sheets schema, and B2AI_SUBSTRATE / B2AI_TOPIC CURIEs on every instance gives four independent layers of standards conformance.

Element 4 splits under the per-sub-element gating: the governance disjunct (embargo plus commercial-licensing restrictions, both read from Element 2 fields) makes oversight and deidentification applicable and both score 1, while the absence of any human participant makes privacy, consent and compensation not applicable. Scoring those three as 0 would have measured the dataset's subject matter rather than its documentation.

correctness_validations.grant_number_format: valid - 1OT2OD032742-01 and 5U54HG012513-02 both parse as NIH awards; a third grants entry carries a fund name rather than an award number

correctness_validations.orcid_format: valid - 46 creator and contact ORCIDs, all in the 0000-0000-0000-000X form

elements.name: Dataset Discovery and Identification
elements.description: Can a user or system discover and uniquely identify this dataset?

sub_elements.name: Persistent Identifier (DOI, RRID, or URI)
sub_elements.evidence: doi: 10.18130/V3/HIGT4C; id: doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C; raw_data_sources carry RRID:CVCL_0419 and RRID:CVCL_B5P3
sub_elements.quality_note: DOI matches the 10.XXXX pattern and the 10.18130 prefix is the University of Virginia Library Dataverse, corroborated by the page host and the citation's named repository. The id is in CURIE form and every file and collection id is a fragment on it. Two Cellosaurus RRIDs additionally identify the source cell lines.

sub_elements.name: Dataset Title and Description Completeness
sub_elements.evidence: title: Cell Maps for Artificial Intelligence - June 2026 Data Release (Beta); description of roughly 1,100 characters naming the three modalities, both cell lines, the treatment conditions and the ten archives
sub_elements.quality_note: Well over the 200-character threshold and dense with specifics: modality by cell line by treatment, distribution venue, and an explicit statement that the release is interim, that computed cell maps are excluded and that some components are embargoed.

sub_elements.name: Keywords or Tags for Searchability
sub_elements.evidence: 31 keywords including AP-MS, SEC-MS, perturb-seq, CRISPR/Cas9, MDA-MB-468, KOLF2.1J, paclitaxel, vorinostat, protein-protein interaction, subcellular imaging
sub_elements.quality_note: Far above the five-keyword threshold and spanning method, cell line, perturbagen, molecular target and program, with common abbreviation and expansion pairs (AP-MS and affinity purification, iPSC and induced pluripotent stem cell) that widen retrieval.

sub_elements.name: Landing Page and Resources (page, hierarchical resources)
sub_elements.evidence: page: https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/dataset.xhtml?persistentId=doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C; file_collections with six collections and ten resources, each carrying name, format, media_type, compression, file_type, md5 and issued
sub_elements.quality_note: A resolvable DOI-keyed landing page plus a two-level resource hierarchy in which every leaf carries a checksum. This is the strongest structural element in the record.

sub_elements.name: Hierarchical Structure (parent datasets, relationships)
sub_elements.evidence: related_datasets: relationship_type is_new_version_of, target_dataset doi:10.18130/V3/K7TGEM; version_access.versions_available lists five releases with DOIs
sub_elements.quality_note: A typed relationship to the immediately preceding release with a resolvable DOI target, and a note saying what the new release adds. The wider release lineage is enumerated with DOIs for four of the five entries.

elements.name: Dataset Access and Retrieval
elements.description: Can the dataset and its associated resources be located, accessed, and downloaded?

sub_elements.name: Access Policy and IP Restrictions Defined
sub_elements.evidence: license_and_use_terms.license_terms spells out CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 obligations; data_use_permission: no_commercial_use; ip_restrictions names UCSD, Stanford and UCSF as commercial-licensing counterparties and the Regents of the University of California as copyright holder
sub_elements.quality_note: The access policy is actionable rather than a license label: attribution, share-alike, no additional legal or technological restrictions, plus who to negotiate with for commercial use and which institution holds copyright over the spatial-proteomics images specifically.

sub_elements.name: Regulatory Restrictions and Confidentiality Level Specified
sub_elements.evidence: confidential_elements: confidential_elements_present true, temporary pre-publication embargo on the KOLF2.1J and MDA-MB-468 perturb-seq components; human_subject_research.regulatory_compliance quotes 'Human Subjects: No' and 'FDA Regulated: No'; sensitive_elements_present false with justification
sub_elements.quality_note: Confidentiality is stated at the component level, naming which parts are embargoed and why the rest is open. The applicable regulatory frameworks are addressed by exclusion with the source's own wording rather than left silent. HIPAA and GDPR are not named, which is correct for a non-human-subject cell-line release.

sub_elements.name: Download URL or Platform Link Available
sub_elements.evidence: page resolves to the Dataverse dataset; distribution_formats.notes describes selecting individual files below the 1.9 GB web download limit from the files table and using the Dataverse Data Access API for programmatic access
sub_elements.quality_note: No download_url slot is populated, but the platform access instructions are concrete and account for the practical obstacle a user will hit, namely that the dataset as a whole exceeds the single-ZIP download limit.

sub_elements.name: Distribution Formats and File Types Specified
sub_elements.evidence: distribution_formats: format ZIP, media_type application/zip; every resource carries format, media_type, compression, file_type (data_file or metadata_file) and md5
sub_elements.quality_note: Container format and MIME type are stated consistently at both dataset and file level, with checksums for verification. The internal data format of each archive is not given, which is recorded as a separate reuse issue under Element 3.

sub_elements.name: Related Datasets and External Resources Linked
sub_elements.evidence: related_datasets links the October 2025 release; external_resources holds five entries covering the CM4AI preprint (doi 10.1101/2024.05.21.589311), the cm4ai.org portal, the Figshare CRISPRi Perturbation Atlas, the Cell Mapping Toolkit on GitHub and Zenodo, and FAIRSCAPE at fairscape.github.io
sub_elements.quality_note: Each external resource carries a note explaining its relation to the release rather than being a bare link, and third_party_sharing separately records the MassIVE deposits of the raw mass-spectrometry data.

elements.name: Data Reuse and Interoperability
elements.description: Is sufficient information provided to reuse and integrate the dataset with others?

sub_elements.name: License Terms Allow Reuse
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets shared condition met: distribution_formats populated, page resolves to a Dataverse landing page, license explicitly permits share and adapt, all ten archives listed with public file access.
sub_elements.evidence: license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; license_and_use_terms.license_terms: 'Users are free to share and adapt the material provided they give appropriate credit... may not use the material for commercial purposes... must distribute contributions under the same license'
sub_elements.quality_note: A named, versioned, machine-recognisable license with its permissions, conditions and prohibitions written out, plus the attribution expectation that publications cite both the related publication and the data collection.

sub_elements.name: Data Formats Are Standardized (encoding, format)
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets shared condition met (see above).
sub_elements.evidence: format: ZIP; media_type: application/zip; compression: zip; no encoding field; no internal data format on any of the ten resources
sub_elements.quality_note: Only the container is documented. ZIP is a standard archive format with a correct MIME type, but the record never states what a user will find inside: no image format for the 12.6 GB of immunofluorescence archives, no mass-spectrometry format for the SEC-MS and AP-MS archives, no matrix or annotated-data format for the perturbation atlas, and no character encoding for any tabular payload. That is not sufficient to plan integration with another dataset, which is what this sub-element measures.

sub_elements.name: Schema or Ontology Conformance Stated
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets shared condition met (see above).
sub_elements.evidence: conforms_to_standard: [RO_CRATE]; conforms_to: 'RO-Crate packaging with provenance graphs and rich metadata, produced using the FAIRSCAPE framework'; conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema; conforms_to_class: Dataset; instances carry B2AI_SUBSTRATE and B2AI_TOPIC CURIEs
sub_elements.quality_note: Four independent conformance layers: a packaging standard, a named framework producing it, a resolvable metadata schema with the class named, and controlled-vocabulary CURIEs on every instance type.

sub_elements.name: Variable Metadata with Identifiers Defined
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets shared condition met (see above).
sub_elements.evidence: No variables field anywhere in the record
sub_elements.quality_note: The instances block names five instance types with substrate and topic CURIEs, which characterises modality rather than variables. No column, field or measurement definitions, no identifiers for measured entities, and no pointer to a data dictionary inside the release metadata archive.

sub_elements.name: Use Guidance Provided (intended, prohibited uses)
sub_elements.evidence: intended_uses: four use_category entries including AI model training, cellular process analysis and analysis of architectural change under disease, treatment or perturbation; prohibited_uses: 'not to be used in clinical decision-making or in any context involving patient care without appropriate regulatory oversight and approval'
sub_elements.quality_note: Both the permitted and the forbidden direction are stated, and the prohibition carries its reason and its condition for lifting rather than being a flat ban. discouraged_uses is absent, which is the only gap.

elements.name: Ethical Use and Privacy Safeguards
elements.description: Does the dataset provide clear information about consent, privacy, and ethical oversight?

sub_elements.name: IRB or Ethics Review and Data Protection Impact
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Governance disjunct satisfied from Element 2 fields: confidential_elements records a temporary pre-publication embargo that actually applies to named components, and ip_restrictions imposes a commercial-use licensing constraint naming three institutions. These are constraints in force, not a record that no restriction applies. The human-participant disjunct is not satisfied (description and keywords name only cell lines; collection_mechanisms describe bench assays). No Element 4 field was used to reach this determination.
sub_elements.evidence: ethical_reviews: two named ethical review contacts from the release record's Data Governance and Ethics section, Vardit Ravitsky (ORCID:0000-0002-7080-8801) and Jean-Christophe Belisle-Pipon (ORCID:0000-0002-8965-8153), each with email and affiliation; data_governance.committee_name 'Data Governance Committee' with contact Jillian Parker (ORCID:0000-0003-4535-3486, UCSD); data_governance.notes records the planned Data Access Committee for distribution and dual-licensing oversight
sub_elements.quality_note: Ethical oversight is documented in exactly the form the sub-element names for a dataset of this kind: governance committee contacts and named ethics review contacts, each identified by ORCID and institution. Each identity resolution is caveated where the record inferred it from a surname and initial match, and one caveat honestly flags that Ravitsky's stated affiliation and email domain differ. No IRB approval is cited, which is correct rather than missing, because no human subjects are involved.

sub_elements.name: Deidentification Method Described
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same governance disjunct as sub-element 1: the embargo in confidential_elements and the commercial-licensing restriction in ip_restrictions are Element 2 constraints in force. Deidentification is meaningful for donor-derived material even with no human participants, which is why this sub-element carries the governance disjunct.
sub_elements.evidence: is_deidentified: identifiable_elements_present false, with 'The release record answers De-identified Samples: Yes' and the preprint's statement that CM4AI data are non-clinical, from tissue cultures, and are considered to be de-identified as they cannot be matched, with current knowledge, to a human subject; raw_data_sources give the commercial provenance of both lines, ATCC and HipSci
sub_elements.quality_note: The approach is a provenance argument rather than a named technique, and for commercially distributed established cell lines that is the semantically appropriate account: the material arrives de-identified and the non-linkability claim is stated with its epistemic hedge. Sourcing to ATCC and HipSci makes the claim checkable, and known_biases separately records the donor characteristics that constitute the residual identifiability context. A named standard such as HIPAA Safe Harbor would be the wrong instrument here.

sub_elements.name: Privacy Protections and Re-identification Risk Assessment
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: No human participants. description and keywords (E1) reference only MDA-MB-468 and KOLF2.1J cell lines with no participant, patient or clinical-research term; collection_mechanisms (E8) describe AP-MS, SEC-MS, immunofluorescence and CRISPRi assays on cultured lines with no recruitment; direct_collection.is_direct is false, stating that data were not collected from individuals. Per #1060 the governance structure present here (embargo, data access committee, governance contact) is not a participant signal and does not make this sub-element applicable.
sub_elements.evidence: Not scored. Excluded from the denominator.
sub_elements.quality_note: There are no participants whose privacy could be protected or whose re-identification risk could be assessed. Scoring this 0 would measure the dataset's subject matter rather than the quality of its documentation.

sub_elements.name: Informed Consent Obtained from Participants
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: No human participants, on the same Element 1 and Element 8 evidence as sub-element 3. The governance structure is not a participant signal (#1060).
sub_elements.evidence: Not scored. Excluded from the denominator.
sub_elements.quality_note: No participants were enrolled, so there is no consent procedure, consent type or withdrawal mechanism to document. Consent for the original cell-line donations sits with ATCC and HipSci, outside this dataset's documentation obligation.

sub_elements.name: Vulnerable Populations and Compensation Documented
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: No human participants, on the same Element 1 and Element 8 evidence as sub-element 3. The governance structure is not a participant signal (#1060).
sub_elements.evidence: Not scored. Excluded from the denominator.
sub_elements.quality_note: No participants were recruited, so there is no at-risk population to protect and no compensation to report.

elements.name: Data Composition and Structure
elements.description: Can the dataset's structure, modality, and population be understood from metadata?

sub_elements.name: Cohort or Subpopulations Characteristics Described
sub_elements.evidence: raw_data_sources characterise both lines: MDA-MB-468 (RRID:CVCL_0419) 'established from a metastatic site pleural effusion of a 51-year-old black female with a metastatic mammary adenocarcinoma', KOLF2.1J (RRID:CVCL_B5P3) 'derived from a healthy male Northern European donor'; known_biases.affected_subsets repeats both characterisations; sampling_strategies give the targeted set of 100 chromatin modifiers and 100 metabolic enzymes
sub_elements.quality_note: The subpopulations slot itself is absent, but the biological populations of a cell-line dataset are characterised with the specificity the sub-element asks for: donor demographics and disease state for both lines, the differentiation states (undifferentiated iPSC, neural progenitor, neuron, cardiomyocyte), the treatment arms (untreated, paclitaxel, vorinostat), and the inclusion criterion for the targeted gene set.

sub_elements.name: Number of Instances or Samples Reported
sub_elements.evidence: total_file_count: 10, reconciling with six collection file_count values; per-archive sizes from 30.2 KB to 4.6 GB in the collection descriptions; sampling_strategies report the KOLF2.1J atlas as covering 11,739 targeted genes; notes give project-level holdings of 1,374 protein interactions, 53,788 immunofluorescent images and 7,023 proteins
sub_elements.quality_note: Extent is quantified at file level exactly and at content level for the KOLF2.1J component. The project-level figures are reported with an explicit caveat that reading them as cumulative across all CM4AI streams is this record's inference, so they are not passed off as release counts. Per-archive instance counts for this release are the residual gap, and the record says why: the June 2026 listing carries no per-file descriptions.

sub_elements.name: Variable-Level Metadata and Tabular Flag
sub_elements.evidence: No variables field and no is_tabular field anywhere in the record
sub_elements.quality_note: Neither a data dictionary nor a tabular indicator is present, and nothing points to where one might be found inside the release metadata archive. For a release spanning transcriptomics, elution profiles and imaging this is the largest structural omission.

sub_elements.name: Data Topics or Conditions Represented
sub_elements.evidence: instances: five entries covering immunofluorescence confocal images under three treatment conditions, SEC-MS elution profiles, AP-MS interaction measurements, single-cell CRISPRi perturbation profiles and raw sequence read sets, each with data_substrate and data_topic CURIEs (B2AI_SUBSTRATE:19/58/59/63/64, B2AI_TOPIC:19/26/28/34)
sub_elements.quality_note: Every modality present in the release is represented as a typed instance with controlled-vocabulary substrate and topic terms, and the disease and perturbation contexts (triple-negative breast cancer, paclitaxel, vorinostat, CRISPRi knockdown, iPSC differentiation) are carried in the instance descriptions.

sub_elements.name: Data Quality Issues and Anomalies Documented
sub_elements.evidence: sampling_strategies: two entries with is_sample, is_random and strategy text, each carrying source_caveats that flag conflicting protein counts between the portal (523) and the October 2025 release page (464) and that mark the is_sample false value as the record's own reading; known_limitations records that the SEC-MS, imaging and perturb-seq data interrogate incompletely overlapping protein sets
sub_elements.quality_note: Sampling is documented in depth, including the record's own uncertainty about whether the genome-scale CRISPRi coverage constitutes a sample. The incomplete cross-modality overlap is the substantive data-quality issue for this release and it is stated plainly. The anomalies slot itself is empty and missing_data_documentation is absent, so the coverage comes from adjacent fields rather than the primary one.

sub_elements.name: Dataset Version Number Provided
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets shared condition met: distribution_formats populated, resolvable Dataverse landing page, license permits reuse.
sub_elements.evidence: version: '2.0'; status: Beta; citation ends 'University of Virginia Dataverse, V2'
sub_elements.quality_note: A version number and a maturity status, agreeing with the version recorded in the citation string. The cross-release version numbering oddity is noted as a separate low-severity issue.

sub_elements.name: Version Access Methods Documented
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets shared condition met (see above).
sub_elements.evidence: version_access.latest_version_doi: doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C; versions_available lists the June 2026, October 2025 (doi 10.18130/V3/K7TGEM), June 2025 (doi 10.18130/V3/F3TD5R), March 2025 (doi 10.18130/V3/B35XWX) and May 2024 releases; version_details explains that each quarterly release is deposited under its own DOI and separately versioned within Dataverse
sub_elements.quality_note: The access route to each prior version is a resolvable DOI, and the record explains the versioning scheme rather than only listing versions, which is what a user needs to navigate a DOI-per-release arrangement.

sub_elements.name: Change Descriptions and Errata Provided
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets shared condition met (see above).
sub_elements.evidence: related_datasets notes: 'The June 2026 release adds AP-MS data for treated MDA-MB-468 breast cancer cells, which the October 2025 release did not include'; source_caveats records that the June 2026 immunofluorescence archives carry different MD5 checksums from the identically named October 2025 archives, that the description text ends with a trailing 2025-06-30 stamp carried forward from earlier releases, and that three archives were published a month after the release date
sub_elements.quality_note: A concrete delta against the immediately preceding release, plus four errata-grade observations about the release record itself: changed checksums under unchanged file names, carried-forward description text, a date conflict between portal and repository, and post-dated file publication. No errata slot and no formal changelog, so the material is distributed across notes and caveats rather than collected.

sub_elements.name: Update Schedule or Frequency Indicated
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets shared condition met (see above).
sub_elements.evidence: updates.frequency: Quarterly; updates.update_details: 'regularly updated and augmented through the end of the project in November 2026, with updates on a quarterly basis'
sub_elements.quality_note: Both a cadence and an end date for the maintenance commitment, corroborated from two sources (the release record and the project portal), which tells a user how long to expect new releases and when to stop waiting.

sub_elements.name: Provenance and Source Derivation Documented
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets shared condition met (see above).
sub_elements.evidence: raw_data_sources give both cell lines with RRIDs, source_type and access_details; raw_sources list five external raw deposits in MassIVE and the in-release raw sequence archive; acquisition_methods carry was_directly_observed and was_inferred_derived flags; conforms_to names RO-Crate provenance graphs produced with FAIRSCAPE; third_party_sharing records the external deposits
sub_elements.quality_note: Provenance runs in both directions from the release: back to the two source cell lines with resolvable identifiers and access terms, and out to the MassIVE and Figshare deposits holding the corresponding raw data. Derivation is flagged structurally on the acquisition entries rather than only in prose. The was_derived_from and release_notes slots are unused, but the information they would carry is present elsewhere.

elements.name: Scientific Motivation and Funding Transparency
elements.description: Does the metadata clearly state why the dataset exists and who funded it?

sub_elements.name: Motivation or Purpose for Dataset Creation
sub_elements.evidence: purposes: three responses, including 'machine-readable hierarchical maps of cell architecture as AI-Ready data, produced from multimodal interrogation of 100 chromatin modifiers and 100 metabolic enzymes'; addressing_gaps: two responses on black-box genotype-phenotype models and on the absence of AI-Ready properties in existing biomedical data
sub_elements.quality_note: Purpose is stated at three levels of granularity and paired with an explicit account of the research gaps addressed, including a definition of what AI-Ready means to this project: FAIR, known provenance, validated, machine-readable computational provenance, explainable within stated limits, ethically obtained.

sub_elements.name: Primary Research Objectives or Tasks
sub_elements.evidence: tasks: 'Interpretable genotype-phenotype learning, in which predictions are traced to multi-scale cell and tissue architecture rather than produced by an opaque model' and 'Development of visible machine learning systems, including visible neural networks built directly on knowledge maps of cell and tissue architecture'
sub_elements.quality_note: Two named machine-learning objectives that are specific to this dataset's design rather than generic, and that connect directly to the addressing_gaps statement about black-box models.

sub_elements.name: Funding Sources and Mechanisms Listed
sub_elements.evidence: funders: National Institutes of Health with the Bridge2AI Functional Genomics award and the Bridge2AI Bridge Center award, and the University of Virginia Frederick Thomas Fund; notes name Trey Ideker at UCSD as principal investigator per NIH RePORTER
sub_elements.quality_note: Two funders with the mechanism identified for each award (an OT2 Bridge2AI data generation award and a U54 center award), the principal investigator named, and the award amount and project period recorded from RePORTER.

sub_elements.name: Grant IDs or Award Numbers Present
sub_elements.evidence: grant_number: 1OT2OD032742-01, with the note recording the RePORTER core project number OT2OD032742, application 11211616, supplement 3OT2OD032742-01S2, award amount 5,289,382 and project period 2022-09-01 to 2026-08-31; grant_number: 5U54HG012513-02
sub_elements.quality_note: Both NIH numbers parse against the expected pattern: type digit, activity code (OT2, U54), institute code (OD, HG), serial and support year. The first is corroborated against RePORTER with its core project number, supplement and period. The third grants entry holds a fund name rather than a number, which is a form issue the record itself flags.

sub_elements.name: Creators and Acknowledgements Documented
sub_elements.evidence: creators: 46 entries, 41 with ORCID identifiers, each with an institutional affiliation spanning UCSD, UCSF, Stanford, University of Virginia, KTH, Yale, UAB, Simon Fraser, University of Montreal and University of Texas at Austin; maintainers name the CM4AI Program Manager and website support contact
sub_elements.quality_note: Near-complete ORCID coverage across a large author list with affiliations, matching the citation string. Institutional support is acknowledged through the maintainers block and the funder notes.

elements.name: Technical Transparency (Data Collection and Processing)
elements.description: Can data collection and processing steps be replicated or understood?

sub_elements.name: Collection Mechanisms and Settings Described
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Data collection identified (acquisition_methods and collection_mechanisms populated) and the datasets shared condition is met.
sub_elements.evidence: collection_mechanisms: four entries covering AP-MS on endogenously tagged cell lines, SEC-MS for proteome-wide complex mapping, immunofluorescence staining and confocal microscopy using Human Protein Atlas antibodies with automated fixation and permeabilization protocols established for both lines, and single-cell CRISPRi screens using the 10x Genomics 3'HT kit with a lentiviral library and inducible dCas9 cell lines; data_collectors name four production sites with roles; collection_timeframes give the creation and deposit dates and the award period
sub_elements.quality_note: Each mechanism carries the technical specifics a replicator would need: the tagging strategy, the antibody resource, the interference system and the commercial kit. Site-to-modality attribution is provided with an honest caveat that the June 2026 listing names production locations collectively and the assignment is drawn from the preprint and earlier release pages.

sub_elements.name: Data Acquisition Methods Listed
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Data collection identified and datasets shared condition met (see above).
sub_elements.evidence: acquisition_methods: a primary-measurement entry with was_directly_observed true and was_reported_by_subjects false, listing AP-MS, SEC-MS, immunofluorescence confocal microscopy and single-cell CRISPR screens, and a derived-processing entry with was_inferred_derived true; raw_data_sources give both cell lines with RRIDs and repositories; raw_sources list the MassIVE deposits
sub_elements.quality_note: Instruments and assays are enumerated and the structural flags correctly separate direct observation from derivation. The derived entry is explicitly marked as inferred from paired archive names, so the reader can tell which part of the acquisition account is evidenced and which is reconstructed.

sub_elements.name: Preprocessing, Cleaning, Labeling, and Annotation Quality
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Software condition satisfied from Element 10 fields: external_resources names the Cell Mapping Toolkit / CM4AI data integration pipeline released under BSD-3 via GitHub with tools archived in Zenodo, and the FAIRSCAPE framework at fairscape.github.io. No Element 8 field was used to reach this determination.
sub_elements.evidence: preprocessing_strategies: one entry, 'Perturb-seq data are distributed both as a processed CRISPRi perturbation cell atlas and as the underlying raw sequence data, in separate archives', with source_caveats 'Inferred from archive naming in the June 2026 file listing; that listing carries no per-file processing description'
sub_elements.quality_note: The only preprocessing statement in the record is an inference from two file names, and the record says so. No pipeline steps, no parameters, no cleaning, no labeling method, no annotation quality analysis, no machine annotation tools and no imputation protocol. A reuser cannot tell what was done to the data between instrument and archive, which is what this sub-element measures. The record does note that computed cell maps are produced by self-supervised multimodal embedding and multi-resolution community detection, but those outputs are excluded from this release.

sub_elements.name: Software and Tools Documented
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same software condition as sub-element 3, satisfied from external_resources (Element 10).
sub_elements.evidence: No software_and_tools field. Software appears only inside external_resources: 'Cell Mapping Toolkit / CM4AI data integration pipeline software, released under a BSD-3 open source license via GitHub, with production-ready tools archived in Zenodo' and 'FAIRSCAPE AI-readiness framework, https://fairscape.github.io'
sub_elements.quality_note: Two software artefacts are named with their licenses and hosting venues, but no version is given for either, the GitHub repository is described rather than linked, and neither is tied to the production of the archives in this release. The toolkit is the integration pipeline for computed cell maps, which this release explicitly excludes, so it does not document the processing of the data actually distributed.

sub_elements.name: External Standards and Resources Referenced
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets shared condition met (see Element 3).
sub_elements.evidence: external_resources: the CM4AI preprint (doi 10.1101/2024.05.21.589311) with its full author list, the cm4ai.org portal, the Figshare CRISPRi Perturbation Atlas, the Cell Mapping Toolkit, and FAIRSCAPE; existing_uses cites the iPSC perturbation atlas preprint (doi 10.1101/2024.11.03.621734, PMC11580897); conforms_to and conforms_to_standard name RO-Crate and FAIRSCAPE
sub_elements.quality_note: Two publications with resolvable DOIs and one with a PMCID, a project portal, an external data host, and two named standards or frameworks, each entry annotated with its relation to the release.

elements.name: Dataset Evaluation and Limitations Disclosure
elements.description: Does the metadata communicate known risks, biases, or dataset limitations?

sub_elements.name: Known Limitations Documented
sub_elements.evidence: known_limitations: six typed entries covering scope (interim release, not final form), coverage (predicted cell maps absent; perturb-seq components embargoed), integration (SEC-MS, imaging and perturb-seq interrogate incompletely overlapping protein sets; the release is most suitable for single-modality bioinformatics rather than cross-modality analysis) and methodology (meaningful analysis requires domain expertise)
sub_elements.quality_note: Each limitation is typed with a controlled limitation_type and states a consequence for the user rather than a disclaimer. The integration limitation is the one that most affects reuse and it is stated twice, once as a fact about protein-set overlap and once as a recommendation about what analysis the release supports.

sub_elements.name: Biases Categorized Using Standard Taxonomy (RAI-aligned)
sub_elements.evidence: known_biases: bias_type representation_bias, description 'derived from commercially available de-identified human cell lines and do not represent all biological variants which may be seen in the population at large', affected_subsets naming all modalities and the donor characteristics of both lines
sub_elements.quality_note: A BiasTypeEnum category is used rather than free text, the affected scope is stated as all modalities, and the description grounds the bias in the specific donor demographics of the two lines. Only one bias category is present and future_use_impacts is absent, so anticipated downstream social impacts are not covered, but the bias that is documented is the one that genuinely applies to a two-cell-line release.

sub_elements.name: Data Anomalies and Quality Issues Noted
sub_elements.evidence: source_caveats records the portal-versus-Dataverse release date conflict, the trailing 2025-06-30 stamp indicating description text carried forward between releases, three immunofluorescence archives published a month after the release date, and the absence of per-file descriptions in the June 2026 listing; file_collections source_caveats records that the June 2026 immunofluorescence archives carry different MD5 checksums from identically named October 2025 archives; sampling_strategies records the 523-versus-464 protein count conflict
sub_elements.quality_note: Six distinct irregularities are documented with enough detail for a user to act on them, and the checksum finding is materially useful: identically named archives across two releases are not the same bytes. These are metadata-level anomalies rather than data-level ones, and the anomalies slot itself is empty, so the coverage is real but sits in the wrong fields.

sub_elements.name: Sensitive Content and Warnings Provided
sub_elements.evidence: sensitive_elements: sensitive_elements_present false, with 'the release record states that the dataset does not involve human subjects, that samples are de-identified, and that the data are not FDA regulated' and the preprint's statement that CM4AI data are non-clinical, deriving from tissue cultures; confidential_elements records the pre-publication embargo on named components
sub_elements.quality_note: The negative determination is reasoned and sourced rather than asserted, resting on three separate release-record answers plus the preprint. The embargo is recorded separately as the access-side sensitivity that does apply, so the record distinguishes 'no sensitive content' from 'no restrictions'.

sub_elements.name: Ethical Review Details Including Conflicts
sub_elements.evidence: ethical_reviews: two entries, each naming an ethical review contact from the release record's Data Governance and Ethics section with ORCID, email and affiliation, and each carrying a source_caveats explaining how the contact was matched to the author list; data_governance names the Data Governance Committee, its contact and the planned Data Access Committee overseeing distribution and potential dual licensing
sub_elements.quality_note: Ethics review is documented as named, contactable people with persistent identifiers, and the record is candid about the inference used to resolve each identity, including the mismatch between Ravitsky's stated affiliation and email domain. Conflicts of interest are not disclosed, which is the one component of this sub-element left uncovered.

elements.name: Cross-Platform and Community Integration
elements.description: Does the dataset connect to wider data ecosystems, repositories, or standards?

sub_elements.name: Dataset Published on a Recognized Platform
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets shared condition met (see Element 3).
sub_elements.evidence: page host dataverse.lib.virginia.edu; citation names 'University of Virginia Dataverse'; maintainers record long-term preservation by the University of Virginia Dataverse (LibraData) supported by committed institutional funds; distribution_formats.notes describe the Dataverse files table and Data Access API
sub_elements.quality_note: The publishing platform is a recognised institutional repository, identified consistently across four independent fields and corroborated by the DOI prefix. The publisher slot itself is not populated, but the platform is unambiguous and the preservation commitment behind it is stated.

sub_elements.name: Citation and DOI for Cross-referencing
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Publication identified (citation populated; external_resources and existing_uses carry two preprint DOIs) and the datasets shared condition is met.
sub_elements.evidence: citation: the full Dataverse citation with all 46 authors, year 2026, title, https://doi.org/10.18130/V3/HIGT4C, repository and version V2; doi: 10.18130/V3/HIGT4C
sub_elements.quality_note: A complete, repository-generated citation string that a user can paste, agreeing with the doi, version and title fields elsewhere in the record. license_and_use_terms additionally states the expectation that publications cite both the related publication and the data collection.

sub_elements.name: Community Standards or Schema Conformance
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets shared condition met (see Element 3).
sub_elements.evidence: conforms_to_standard: [RO_CRATE]; conforms_to: RO-Crate packaging with provenance graphs, produced using the FAIRSCAPE framework; conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema; conforms_to_class: Dataset; B2AI_SUBSTRATE and B2AI_TOPIC CURIEs on every instance
sub_elements.quality_note: RO-Crate is a genuine community packaging standard and FAIRSCAPE a named framework implementing it, both paired with a resolvable metadata schema and a controlled vocabulary applied at instance level. This is standards conformance asserted at four layers rather than a single label.

sub_elements.name: Outreach Materials and Documentation Links
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets shared condition met (see Element 3).
sub_elements.evidence: page: the Dataverse landing page; external_resources: CM4AI project portal at https://cm4ai.org/ described as providing documentation, data release listings, tools and publications, and FAIRSCAPE at https://fairscape.github.io; two preprints with DOIs; the Figshare-hosted CRISPRi Perturbation Atlas
sub_elements.quality_note: A landing page plus a project portal that is explicitly characterised as the documentation and release-listing entry point, and a framework documentation site. No webinars or tutorials are named, so outreach is covered by documentation links rather than training material.

sub_elements.name: Related Datasets with Typed Relationships
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets shared condition met (see Element 3).
sub_elements.evidence: related_datasets: relationship_type is_new_version_of, target_dataset doi:10.18130/V3/K7TGEM, with a note stating what this release adds relative to that one
sub_elements.quality_note: The relationship is typed with a controlled term and points at a resolvable DOI, and the note makes the relation substantive by naming the AP-MS addition. Only one typed relation is present: the three earlier releases appear in version_access without relationship types, and the MassIVE and Figshare deposits are carried in raw_sources and external_resources rather than as typed relations, so the relationship graph is thinner than the release lineage would support.

strengths: Identifier and platform integrity is complete and self-corroborating: a valid Dataverse DOI whose 10.18130 prefix matches the landing page host and the citation's named repository, a CURIE-form record id that every collection and file id is a fragment on, MD5 checksums on all ten archives, and a total_file_count that reconciles exactly with the six collection counts.

The record is unusually disciplined about the boundary between what its sources state and what it inferred. Twelve source_caveats blocks flag a portal-versus-repository date conflict and how it was resolved by source rank, a 523-versus-464 protein count conflict left unasserted, an is_sample value identified as the record's own reading, laboratory-to-modality attributions drawn from the preprint rather than the release listing, and identity matches made on surname and initial, including one where affiliation and email domain disagree.

Ethical and governance documentation is appropriate to a cell-line dataset rather than borrowed from a human-subject template: four mutually consistent negative determinations on human subjects, direct collection, sensitive elements and identifiability, each sourced; named ethics review and governance committee contacts with ORCIDs; and a deidentification claim grounded in commercial cell-line provenance from ATCC and HipSci.

Provenance runs in both directions from the release, back to two RRID-identified cell lines with their repositories and access terms, and outward to the MassIVE mass-spectrometry deposits and the Figshare perturbation atlas, with derivation flagged structurally on the acquisition entries and the whole packaged under RO-Crate provenance graphs.

Funding transparency is complete and validates cleanly: two NIH awards that both parse against the expected activity-institute-serial pattern, the first corroborated against RePORTER with its core project number, supplement, award amount and project period, plus the named principal investigator and 41 of 46 creators carrying ORCIDs.

Version and release management is documented as a system, not a number: five releases enumerated with four DOIs, an explanation that each quarterly release is a separate Dataverse deposit with its own version counter, a quarterly cadence with a stated end date, and a concrete statement of what this release adds relative to its predecessor.
weaknesses: No variable-level metadata of any kind. The variables and is_tabular slots are both empty and nothing points to a data dictionary inside the release metadata archive, so a user cannot learn what fields the transcriptomic, elution-profile or imaging data contain.

Distribution is documented only at the container level. Every format is ZIP and every media_type application/zip, with no encoding and no statement of the data format inside any archive, so a reuser cannot tell what they will be able to read after unzipping 12.6 GB of imaging data.

Processing is effectively undocumented. The single preprocessing_strategies entry is an inference from two file names, which the record itself says, and there is no cleaning, labeling, annotation-quality, machine-annotation or imputation information anywhere.

Software is named but not usable as documentation: the Cell Mapping Toolkit and FAIRSCAPE appear with licenses and hosting venues but no versions and no repository URL for the toolkit, and neither is tied to producing the archives in this release, since the integration pipeline generates the computed cell maps that this release excludes.

Release-level extent is not asserted. The instance counts in notes are project-wide by the record's own inference and the portal's gene and protein figures are explicitly not claimed for this release, so extent is available as ten archives with byte sizes plus one gene count rather than as counts of images, profiles or cells.

Several structural slots are bypassed while their content sits elsewhere: anomalies is empty with the irregularities in source_caveats, publisher is empty with the repository named in four other fields, subpopulations is empty with the cell-line characterisation in raw_data_sources, and one grants entry carries a fund name in the grant_number slot.
recommendations: Populate variables for at least the tabular components and set is_tabular per collection, or add a pointer from each file_collections entry to the corresponding data dictionary inside cm4ai_release_metadata.zip, which is the single change that would most improve reuse.
State the internal data format for each archive alongside the ZIP container, with character encoding for any tabular or text payload, so that format describes the data rather than only the packaging.

Replace the inferred preprocessing entry with the processing steps recorded in the RO-Crate provenance graphs the release already packages, and add cleaning, labeling and annotation-quality information where the pipeline produced it.

Give the Cell Mapping Toolkit a repository URL and a version or Zenodo DOI, and state which archives in this release each named tool actually produced, so software documentation attaches to distributed data rather than to excluded outputs.

Add a version_details sentence explaining that the Dataverse version counter is per-DOI and does not order releases, since this release at version 2.0 currently appears to precede two predecessors recorded at version 2.1.
Move the Frederick Thomas Fund from grant_number to the grant notes and leave grant_number absent, so that the identifier slot holds only award identifiers.
Record the July 2026 immunofluorescence file additions as a distinct distribution event rather than leaving three file issued dates ahead of the dataset's own publication date.
